children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

First, let me start with a basic question:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 3 years old. He lives at home with me here in the UK. I'm just wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me make sure I understand your situation correctly:

- You have one child named Alex
- Alex is 3 years old
- Alex lives at home with you in the UK

That's a good start. Now I need to ask a few more questions to fully assess your eligibility:

**Are you currently living in the UK yourself?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're both here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. So you and Alex both live together in Manchester, UK.

Let me ask another important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status that gives you the right to live here?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure what you mean by "right to reside" - I live here in Manchester, is that what you're asking?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand the confusion - let me clarify. What I'm asking is about your citizenship or immigration status. This helps determine eligibility for Child Benefit.

**Are you a British citizen, or were you born in the UK? Or if not, are you from another country and have permission to live in the UK (such as having a visa, settled status, or indefinite leave to remain)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see what you mean now. Yes, I'm a British citizen - born and raised here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex in any of these situations:**
- Currently in hospital or residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks?
- In local council care for more than 8 weeks?
- Living with someone else (not with you)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. Alex lives at home with me full-time, and he's not in hospital or in any kind of care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 3 years old (under 16)
- You're responsible for Alex and he lives with you full-time in the UK
- You're a British citizen living in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- There are no special circumstances affecting eligibility

You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. 

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you can still claim the benefit if you wish.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
